subject: Recap + MAP: technical evaluation milestones & benchmark targets
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <s.jones@healthgrid.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Technical evaluation next steps & draft MAP milestone

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Per our call I captured a focused technical-eval MAP milestone and a set of concrete targets so your engineering team can validate fit. Attached: HealthGrid_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft) and tech-benchmark-spec.md (benchmark spec).

High-level ask: confirm right people and a target close date for the MAP so we can reserve dedicated infra for the run. Proposed target close date for the MAP: 2027-06-03.

Draft MAP milestone (technical evaluation) — summary:
- Objective: Validate Redwood inference meets HealthGrid latency/cost and quality thresholds on representative workload.
- Owner (Redwood): Olga Petrov — coordinate infra, model config, and benchmark harness.
- Owner (HealthGrid): Sarah Jones — provide data sample, acceptance criteria, security signoff.
- Timeline: kickoff week of 4/19, benchmarks run 4/26–5/10, readout 5/17, final decision 6/03.

Benchmark success criteria (please confirm):
1) Quality: automated evals on 1k holdout prompts — target > 92% exact/near-match on labeled set OR human A/B pref >= 60% vs. baseline.
2) Latency: P95 generation latency <= 120ms for 512-token sequences (end-to-end, hosted/Private config).
3) Cost: effective token cost <= $0.15 per 1k tokens on average for target throughput profile.
4) Throughput: sustain 60 inference requests/minute with <= 2% error rate on test harness.

Model shortlist we propose for the technical run (flexible):
- Redwood-verified: redwood/opt-6.7b-quant (fast, quantized)
- Open candidate: open/llama2-13b (baseline quality)
- Experimental: redwood/cerebras-13b (higher perf on long context)
Please flag any model(s) you want added/removed.

Dependencies (blocking items for kickoff):
- Security/compliance questionnaire completion (we need SOC2 attestation + data handling confirmation)
- Access to a ~1k prompt sample (anonymized) and expected output examples via secure S3 link or Drive.
- Network access for Private trial or permission to run on Redwood Dedicated infra (we can provide temporary creds).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm participants and provide procurement contact (so we can add procurement to the MAP and comment on costs).
2) HealthGrid uploads sample to shared Drive or provides S3 read-only link by 4/15.
3) Redwood prepares infra estimate and final benchmark script by 4/18.
4) Kickoff meeting week of 4/19 to lock in exact configs & QA plan.

If this looks good I will update the MAP file and create milestone tasks (owners/dates) and link to the hubspot deal.

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Attachments: HealthGrid_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), tech-benchmark-spec.md (benchmark spec)

From: Sarah Jones <s.jones@healthgrid.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@healthgrid.ai>, procurement@healthgrid.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Technical evaluation next steps & draft MAP milestone

Thanks Olga — this is helpful and aligns with what our engineers want to validate. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Latency target: our initial ask was P95 <= 100ms for 512 tokens if achievable; we can be pragmatic but please call out if that requires higher-cost configs.
- Quality metric: we can share a labeled subset (250 prompts) for the automated eval; for human eval we'll coordinate 3 reviewers.
- Model shortlist: please include an additional smaller/cheaper baseline (eg. redwood/opt-3b-quant) so we can compare cost/quality tradeoffs.

Procurement is cc'ed — procurement@healthgrid.ai will coordinate contract/PO questions. Tom (eng lead) will be the primary technical contact for scheduling and data access; he will send the sample link by 4/15.

Confirming target MAP close date 2027-06-03 — procurement may push on timing, but we'll try to stay on that cadence.

Thanks,
Sarah
Director, Product — HealthGrid

On Apr 10, 2027, at 3:12 PM, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <s.jones@healthgrid.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Technical evaluation next steps & draft MAP milestone

Sarah — thanks for the quick reply. Couple of internal notes/asks from the infra side: 
- If HealthGrid expects P95 <= 100ms for 512 tokens, that typically means using a lower-parameter model or a higher-cost instance profile (we can run both in the MAP). I'll include a short infra-cost comparison in the updated MAP.
- For reproducibility, please indicate expected average prompt length and target distribution (we need token distribution to size KV cache properly).
- Redwood can provide a temporary Dedicated pool for the run (2 nodes) if you want isolation and consistent perf; otherwise we can use hosted with pinned model variant.

I'll update the MAP with two perf profiles ("cost-optimized" and "latency-optimized") and the corresponding infra assumptions.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <s.jones@healthgrid.ai>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@healthgrid.ai>, procurement@healthgrid.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: MAP update: finalized milestone tasks, owners & next meetings (action items)

Following Sarah and Marcus' input I've updated the MAP and attached the new version (HealthGrid_MAP_v1.xlsx) and the benchmark spec. Highlights from the updated MAP: 

1) Milestone tasks (owners / target dates):
- 4/15: HealthGrid provides anonymized prompt sample (owner: Tom Keller).
- 4/18: Redwood delivers benchmark harness & infra estimate (owner: Olga Petrov).
- 4/26–5/10: Benchmark runs (owner: Marcus Lin). Two profiles run in parallel: 
    * Latency-optimized (target P95 <= 100ms) — config: Dedicated 2xA100-like nodes, models: opt-3b-quant, opt-6.7b-quant, llama2-13b.
    * Cost-optimized (target cost <= $0.15 / 1k tokens) — config: hosted quantized instances, models: opt-3b-quant, opt-6.7b-quant.
- 5/17: Readout & qualitative human evaluation (owners: Sarah/Tom + Redwood).
- 6/03: MAP decision meeting (owner: HealthGrid execs).

2) Acceptance criteria (condensed from spec):
- Quality: automated eval >= 92% on labeled subset OR human A/B pref >= 60%.
- Latency: P95 <= 100ms for latency-optimized profile (512 tokens). If missed, note configuration that met 120ms and associated cost delta.
- Cost: cost-optimized runs average <= $0.15 / 1k tokens.

3) Dependencies (status):
- Questionnaire: HealthGrid completed sections 1–3; Sarah noted procurement will finish contract language by 4/20.
- Data: Tom to share sample by 4/15 (pending).
- Infra: Redwood ready to reserve Dedicated pool from 4/25 if HealthGrid confirms.

4) Action items (next week):
- 4/13: 30-min kickoff to align on tokenization & exact prompt set (invite to follow).
- 4/18: Redwood shares benchmark harness + runbook.

If you agree to the updated targets (P95 <=100ms for latency profile, cost <=$0.15 for cost profile), I'll convert the milestones to HubSpot tasks and lock in the Dedicated reservation on our side.

Thank you — looking forward to the kickoff.

Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Attachments: HealthGrid_MAP_v1.xlsx, tech-benchmark-spec.md
